claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'DELETE statement' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Indexed I-O module, IX-21'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'DELETE statement' then '  Indexed I-O module, IX-21'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page B-53 (PDF p965) is an informative index page. The transcription holds one line per entry with the sub-entries indented two spaces beneath their main entry, e.g. 'DELETE statement' / '  Indexed I-O module, IX-21' / '  Relative I-O module, VIII-19'. That mirrors the printed layout. I spot-checked the entries in the left column: DELIMITED BY, Delimiters, DEPENDING, DESCENDING KEY, DIVIDE and DUPLICATES, with their sub-entries and page references. They match, and the claim itself says the entries and references match. The only issue the claim raises is how a Markdown renderer would flow bare lines, which is a formatting and rendering concern. No text is missing, misquoted or changed in meaning. A difference that is only formatting is rejected under the verification rules.
